description: Tests the ORCHESTRATION defined in CLAUDE.md, not agent quality. A real orchestrator session runs the pipeline; the workers (architect/developer/reviewers) are FAKE agent definitions (project-local .claude/agents overrides) that record their own invocation to pipeline-calls.log and return canned artifacts. The fake test-reviewer FORCES a FAIL on the first review (then PASS) so the fix pass is exercised on demand — something real agents won't do reliably. We assert the choreography from the call log: plan before implement, implement before review, FAIL triggers a developer fix pass, re-review after the fix, and it stops after a passing review (no further fix). The orchestrator prompt is deliberately minimal so CLAUDE.md's pipeline rules drive the dance. This is paid + pass@k (the orchestrator is a real model); faking the workers makes it cheap and the FAIL path forceable.
orchestratorPrompt: The feature 'withdraw-money' has its scenarios approved in docs/specifications/withdraw-money/specification.md. Proceed with the implementation pipeline defined in your project instructions (CLAUDE.md): plan and implement each approved scenario, then run the reviewers, and apply the fix pass if a reviewer reports a problem. Use the project's architect, developer, and reviewer sub-agents — do not do their work yourself. Work directly in this directory; skip any worktree step. Run non-interactively: do not ask questions, auto-continue, and stop once the reviewers pass.
